create.name: Thomas Moore
create.bio:
Thomas Moore wrote Care of the Soul, the 1992 book that brought the old idea of tending the soul back into everyday conversation and stayed on the New York Times list for most of a year. In his youth he spent years in a Catholic religious order and trained in composing music; afterwards he earned a doctorate in religious studies at Syracuse, taught at university, and trained as a psychotherapist in the tradition of C. G. Jung and James Hillman. He has since written some thirty books.

His work weaves together spirituality, Greek myth, depth psychology and the arts, and he puts imagination and images at the centre of inner life. Rather than fixing problems, he encourages people to give their ordinary lives more depth: through work, love, ageing, religion of one's own making, and attention to dreams and beauty. He has written fresh translations of the Gospels with commentary, books on silence and emptiness, and a new book on Thoreau. He lectures widely, often online, and teaches Imaginal Psychology, a series of six-week online courses on the soul, myth and archetypes, from his home in New Hampshire.

books.title: The Eloquence of Silence: Discovering the Power of Emptiness
books.author: Thomas Moore
books.description: Draws on Taoist, Buddhist and Christian sources to suggest that emptiness and quiet are not a lack but something to welcome, and that letting go of striving can make life lighter.

books.title: Ageless Soul: The Lifelong Journey Toward Meaning and Joy
books.author: Thomas Moore
books.description: Looks at growing older as a chance to become more fully oneself rather than a loss, with reflections on friendship, purpose, memory and the inner life in later years.

books.title: Gospel: The Book of Mark
books.author: Thomas Moore
books.description: A fresh translation of Mark with commentary that sets aside doctrinal readings and reads the text as a radical picture of how to live, open to readers of any tradition.

books.title: Gospel: The Book of Matthew
books.author: Thomas Moore
books.description: His translation of Matthew with spiritual and psychological notes, bringing out the universal meaning of familiar passages and key words.

books.title: The Book of Job
books.author: Thomas Moore
books.description: An edition of the biblical Book of Job with his introduction, reading the story of loss and questioning through the lens of the soul.

books.title: The Soul of Christmas
books.author: Thomas Moore
books.description: A short book on the images of the Christmas story, from the divine child to the star, as symbols with meaning for people of any faith or none.

courses.title: Imaginal Psychology: online course series
courses.description: A sequence of six online courses, each six weeks long, on the soul, Jung and Hillman, Greek myth, dreams, alchemy and the spiritual traditions. Each week brings short readings, a live talk with questions, and ongoing written conversation among participants; finishing all six earns his certificate.
